title: Outbound traffic from a private subnet
prompt: An application runs on EC2 instances in a private subnet, separate from the public web tier. The instances in the application tier must retrieve update packages without public IP addresses or allowing direct inbound connections from the internet. Select the required changes. Choose two.

choices.text: Place a public NAT gateway in a public subnet
choices.explanation: Place a public NAT gateway in a public subnet and assign it an Elastic IP. The subnet needs a default route to an internet gateway.

choices.text: Point the application tier's default route to the NAT gateway
choices.explanation: This sends outbound traffic from EC2 through the NAT and allows responses to return over the original connection.

choices.text: Assign an Elastic IP to the application-tier EC2 instances
choices.explanation: Assigning an Elastic IP alone does not establish a route from the private subnet.

choices.text: Point the application tier's default route directly to an internet gateway
choices.explanation: An internet gateway does not provide outbound NAT for EC2 instances that have only private IPv4 addresses.

choices.text: Place a NAT instance in the same private subnet as the application tier
choices.explanation: Simply placing it in the same isolated private subnet does not give the NAT instance internet connectivity.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第1問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: Both a NAT placement and an EC2 route configuration are required to provide outbound access without assigning public IP addresses to private EC2 instances.
learning.concept: A public NAT translates the source address. Point the EC2 default route to the NAT, and provide a route from the NAT's subnet to the internet gateway.

check.prompt: Does creating a NAT also change the EC2 route?
check.answer: No. Associate the route table with the EC2 subnet and verify its default route.

title: Preserving EC2 Memory State
prompt: You want to reduce EC2 compute charges while the instance is not in use. When it resumes, the RAM contents held by running processes must be restored. Which procedure meets these requirements?

choices.text: Save the data to instance store and reattach it after stopping the instance
choices.explanation: Instance store data cannot be retained across a stop.

choices.text: Restore from an EBS snapshot
choices.explanation: An EBS snapshot preserves the volume state, but it does not include RAM contents.

choices.text: Hibernate an EC2 instance that supports hibernation
choices.explanation: Hibernation writes RAM to the root EBS volume, and the contents are restored when the instance starts.

choices.text: Stop and start the instance normally in the same Availability Zone
choices.explanation: Keeping the instance in the same Availability Zone does not restore RAM from before a normal stop.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第2問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: Resuming requires the RAM state from before the stop, not just the disk contents.
learning.concept: EC2 hibernation saves RAM contents to the root EBS volume and restores them when the instance resumes. It requires a supported instance type, operating system, and other prerequisites.

check.prompt: Does an EBS snapshot taken before a normal stop include the RAM of running processes?
check.answer: No. A snapshot saves the contents of a volume.

title: Failing Over While Keeping the Same Private IP
prompt: A monitoring client connects to a fixed private IPv4 address. How can you fail over to a standby EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone without changing the destination on the client?

choices.text: Set the primary instance's existing IP as a listener IP on an ALB
choices.explanation: An ALB listener cannot take over the private IP of an existing EC2 instance.

choices.text: Assign the same IP to the standby instance using a DHCP options set
choices.explanation: A DHCP options set cannot be used to switch the private IP assigned to an individual EC2 instance.

choices.text: Move the secondary ENI with the target IP to the standby instance
choices.explanation: In the same Availability Zone, you can move a secondary ENI to another EC2 instance while retaining the IP address on that ENI.

choices.text: Move the primary instance's Elastic IP to the standby instance
choices.explanation: Moving an Elastic IP does not handle traffic addressed to the existing private IPv4 address.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第3問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: The client must continue using the private IP address it already has configured.
learning.concept: A secondary ENI can be moved to another eligible EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Its IP address moves with it. An instance's primary ENI cannot be moved in the same way.

check.prompt: Can you move the ENI as is if the standby server is in a different Availability Zone?
check.answer: No. An ENI can be moved only within the same Availability Zone; a different failover method is needed across Availability Zones.

title: Authenticated GET from a Browser to S3
prompt: A web application's JavaScript makes an authenticated GET request to S3 in a different origin. The request's authentication is already configured. What must be configured so the browser can read the response?

choices.text: Allow the application's origin and GET in the S3 bucket's CORS configuration
choices.explanation: In S3 CORS, allow the web application's origin, GET, and, as needed, headers such as Authorization that are subject to preflight. Request authentication and the browser's CORS check are separate.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning
choices.explanation: Versioning is used to manage object versions.

choices.text: Serve the JavaScript file from a presigned URL
choices.explanation: Changing the URL used to retrieve the script does not add the CORS configuration required for the response from S3 to the application.

choices.text: Allow public execution in the bucket policy
choices.explanation: S3 has no permission that allows code to execute in a browser, and a bucket policy cannot return CORS headers.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第4問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: Passing AWS authentication does not guarantee that a browser can read a response from a different origin.
learning.concept: In S3 CORS, specify the allowed origins and methods, and headers when needed. CORS does not grant access permissions to S3.

check.prompt: Will allowing CORS resolve every S3 403 error?
check.answer: No. Denials caused by a signature, IAM, or a bucket policy must be checked separately.

title: Encrypting S3 Data with Customer-Managed Keys
prompt: Data uploaded to S3 must be encrypted from the time it is first stored. The keys must be kept within the company and must not be stored persistently by AWS. Assume the S3 bucket is already configured to accept SSE-C requests. Which methods meet these requirements? Select two.

choices.text: Encrypt using SSE-S3
choices.explanation: S3 manages the keys used by SSE-S3.

choices.text: Use SSE-KMS with a standard AWS KMS managed key
choices.explanation: This method uses a key managed by AWS KMS for encryption.

choices.text: Use SSE-C and provide the customer's key with each request
choices.explanation: S3 performs server-side encryption and does not store the supplied key persistently.

choices.text: Encrypt on the client with the customer's key before sending the data
choices.explanation: S3 receives encrypted data, and the key can be kept within the company.

choices.text: Upload plaintext, then use an S3 event to invoke Lambda and encrypt the data again
choices.explanation: Even if S3 default encryption applies, the data is not encrypted with the company's key at the time of upload. Re-encrypting it later with Lambda does not meet the requirement.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第5問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: The data must be protected with the company's key from the moment storage begins. One method supplies the key to S3 for each request; the other encrypts the data before it is sent.
learning.concept: With SSE-C, the customer provides the key with each request. With client-side encryption, the data is already ciphertext when sent to S3. If the key is lost, the data cannot be decrypted with either method.

check.prompt: When using SSE-C with S3, is the key needed for a later read?
check.answer: Yes. The matching customer key must be sent so S3 can decrypt the object.

title: A Batch Job That Grows Only at Month-End
prompt: A nightly batch job usually finishes in 7 hours, but the month-end increase is expected to push it past a 10-hour deadline. Once processing starts, it cannot be interrupted. How can you add EC2 capacity for the increased workload while avoiding excess long-term commitments?

choices.text: Add On-Demand Instances at month-end
choices.explanation: You can add capacity only for the period when demand increases, without relying on interruptions caused by Spot reclamation.

choices.text: Purchase Reserved Instances for the additional capacity
choices.explanation: This creates a long-term commitment for capacity needed only briefly each month.

choices.text: Add Spot Instances at month-end
choices.explanation: EC2 can reclaim Spot capacity, so this does not meet the requirement that processing must not be interrupted.

choices.text: Permanently increase the size of the baseline reserved capacity
choices.explanation: You would pay for extra processing capacity even during low-demand periods.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第6問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: The increase occurs only at month-end, and interruptions are not acceptable. Add capacity for the short period while avoiding interruption risk.
learning.concept: On-Demand usage can add capacity without a long-term commitment. Spot capacity may be reclaimed. On-Demand does not guarantee that the capacity you want will be available.

check.prompt: If the batch job could be made restartable, what option would be worth comparing?
check.answer: Spot could be a candidate. Compare completion time and cost, including interruptions and retries.

title: Decoupling a Voting Surge from the Database
prompt: A large number of votes arrive in a short period. When the intake EC2 instances write directly to RDS, the database cannot keep up and vote submissions fail. How can you keep accepting votes during peaks and save them at a rate the database can handle?

choices.text: Move intake to API Gateway and Lambda, and continue writing directly to the database
choices.explanation: Scaling the intake layer does not absorb a surge of direct writes to the database.

choices.text: Use an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment and write to both the primary and standby
choices.explanation: An application cannot use the standby in an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment as a write target.

choices.text: Buffer votes in SQS at intake and save them to RDS with workers whose concurrency is controlled
choices.explanation: The queue absorbs the peak. Account for redelivery by making workers save votes idempotently, using the vote ID.

choices.text: Reconfigure the DB instance each time to match the voting period
choices.explanation: Resizing alone does not control the write rate, and the change method may also require downtime.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第7問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: Absorb the sudden voting surge at the entry point, then send writes to the database at a rate it can process.
learning.concept: Use SQS to decouple intake from persistence. Standard SQS can redeliver messages, so make database writes idempotent using the vote ID or a similar identifier.

check.prompt: What happens if worker concurrency is unlimited?
check.answer: Writes can overwhelm the database, eliminating the benefit of smoothing the load with a queue.

title: Extending the Web and Database Tiers Across AZs
prompt: A deployment with web EC2 instances in public subnets and a self-managed database in private subnets currently runs in a single AZ. The database can be migrated to RDS, and both tiers need to withstand an AZ failure. Which changes are required? Select two.

choices.text: Add public and private subnets in the same AZ
choices.explanation: Adding subnets does not change the impact of an AZ failure.

choices.text: Use a multi-AZ ALB and EC2 Auto Scaling group for the web tier
choices.explanation: Traffic and running instances can be distributed across multiple AZs.

choices.text: Run the current web EC2 instance in its single AZ with an ALB and Auto Scaling
choices.explanation: The web tier would still be confined to one AZ, so it could not continue processing during an AZ-wide failure.

choices.text: Move the database to a single EC2 instance in a public subnet in another AZ
choices.explanation: The database would still be a single instance, and it would no longer be in a private subnet.

choices.text: Provide private subnets in multiple AZs and migrate to an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment
choices.explanation: A standby in another AZ enables failover if the primary fails.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第8問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: Making only one of the web and database tiers redundant does not provide resilience to a single-AZ failure.
learning.concept: Place the ALB and Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs. With an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment, fail over to a standby in another AZ.

check.prompt: Can the standby in a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment serve as a regular read target?
check.answer: No. The standby in this deployment is for availability. Consider a separate option to scale reads.

title: Grace Period for Scale-Out Startup
prompt: Load rises sharply at noon. It takes about 1 minute after adding an EC2 instance before it can handle work, and the existing scaling behavior includes metrics from instances immediately after launch. Which setting would improve scaling decisions?

choices.text: Enable slow start on the NLB target group
choices.explanation: Slow start is an ALB target group feature and does not apply to NLB. Also, adjusting traffic distribution is separate from aggregating Auto Scaling metrics.

choices.text: Add ElastiCache
choices.explanation: A cache can reduce the load from suitable requests, but it does not change how instances are evaluated immediately after launch.

choices.text: Set the instance warmup period in step scaling
choices.explanation: This keeps metrics from instances that are still warming up out of aggregation, reducing fluctuations in scaling decisions caused by values from instances that are not yet ready.

choices.text: Set the ALB as the origin for CloudFront
choices.explanation: This can reduce load from cacheable responses, but it does not change how metrics from EC2 instances that are still starting are evaluated.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第9問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: If scaling decisions use values from just-launched instances, they can be affected by new capacity that is not yet ready to serve work.
learning.concept: Warmup controls when new EC2 instances are included in aggregation. ALB slow start adjusts the share of traffic sent to healthy targets; it is separate from metric aggregation.

check.prompt: Can you use warmup to start EC2 instances ahead of a known business opening time?
check.answer: No. Use scheduled scaling or a similar approach to bring capacity online ahead of a known time.

title: Separating Aurora reads and writes
prompt: Read queries on the Aurora writer are consuming I/O and increasing write latency. How can you offload read processing?

choices.text: Enable a generic read-through cache on the database
choices.explanation: That setting alone does not provide an Aurora feature that routes reads to separate instances.

choices.text: Connect the application directly to a Multi-AZ standby in its standby role
choices.explanation: With Aurora, explicitly add instances for reads and route connections through the appropriate endpoint.

choices.text: Add Aurora Replicas and direct application reads to the reader endpoint
choices.explanation: Add Aurora Replicas and send read connections to the reader endpoint. Connections are distributed; this does not transparently separate reads and writes at the SQL statement level.

choices.text: Create an independent Aurora database, then connect it as a read replica in the same cluster
choices.explanation: An Aurora Replica in the same cluster is configured by adding a DB instance to that cluster.

source.label: AWS公式サンプル 第10問をもとに再構成

learning.reason: Keep writes on the writer and direct only read connections to replicas.
learning.concept: Aurora Replicas share cluster storage with the writer and can serve eventually consistent reads. The reader endpoint distributes new connections.

check.prompt: If you must read an update immediately after an order is placed, where should you read it?
check.answer: When replica lag cannot be tolerated, route the read to the writer as needed.
